title: He was executed for refusing to abandon his faith. Every November 24, Sikhs mark the day he chose it anyway.

sources.text: Tribune India - 350 years of the Guru Tegh Bahadur's martyrdom
SikhiWiki - Martyrdom of Guru Tegh Bahadur

caption:
He was executed for refusing to abandon his faith. Every November 24, Sikhs mark the day he chose it anyway.

His martyrdom is commemorated every year on November 24 as Shaheedi Divas - the fixed date set by the Nanakshahi calendar - after he refused to convert and chose execution over abandoning his faith.

Guru Tegh Bahadur's stand is remembered as a defense of religious freedom broadly, not only for Sikhs - a sacrifice made on behalf of people outside his own community who were facing the same pressure to convert.

Shaheedi Divas is marked across India every year as a reminder that religious freedom in India has always had defenders willing to risk everything for it.
